title: ENTO: an ENcrypted, Typed, Omnitrack container format for multimodal research data
description:
ENTO (ENcrypted, Typed, Omnitrack) is a flat ZIP container format and reference implementation for bundling heterogeneous research artifacts — time series, genomics slices, spectrograms, provenance proofs — into a single verifiable file. Each track is sealed under per-track AES-256-GCM authenticated encryption with format+track associated-data binding and PADMÉ length padding. The default wire format is 0.4.0; formats 0.2.0, 0.3.0, and 0.3.1 remain read/write compatibility profiles. Graded observability levels control how much manifest metadata a recipient sees, and an optional hash-chained proof export provides tamper-evident lineage. Verification deliberately separates key-authenticated integrity from keyless corruption detection.

This deposit is the 0.4 manuscript release candidate together with the MIT-licensed reference implementation source. Planned code home: https://github.com/docxology/entofile.

methods.name: Flat ZIP layout: manifest.json, one encrypted member per track, optional proof
methods.description: Defines the container as a ZIP archive with a typed manifest, per-track .ento members and an optional hash-chain proof file.
methods.evidence: Concretely, an ENTO file is a ZIP archive holding a single manifest.json, one encrypted tracks/{id}.ento member per track, and an optional proof/chain.json.

methods.name: Per-track AES-256-GCM envelopes with HKDF-derived keys
methods.description: Each track is sealed with authenticated encryption under a fixed nonce||tag||ciphertext header, specified in a Kaitai Struct file.
methods.evidence: Per-track authenticated envelope — Fixed header (nonce || tag || ciphertext) with HKDF-derived keys

methods.name: Four graded observability levels for export-time manifest redaction
methods.description: Observability levels 0–3 control which manifest metadata a recipient sees, without re-encrypting the track payloads.
methods.evidence: Graded export — observability levels redact manifests without re-encrypting payloads (sec. 5).

methods.name: Associated-data binding and PADMÉ length padding in the default profile
methods.description: The 0.4.0 default binds associated data and pads ciphertext members to PADMÉ buckets to coarsen the length channel.
methods.evidence: The default profile includes associated-data binding [McGrew, 2008] and PADMÉ length padding [Nikitin et al., 2019], bounding the on-disk ciphertext member-size channel to a coarse bucket.

methods.name: Scripted benchmark: 150 repetitions over observability levels on fixture tracks
methods.description: Benchmarks on committed EEG, VCF and spectrogram fixtures plus a synthetic throughput track measure throughput, latency, expansion and tamper detection.
methods.evidence: This configuration runs 150 repetitions across observability levels 0,1,2,3.

key_findings: Tamper detection succeeded on all 2400 benchmark rows (rate 1.0).
Mean pack throughput was 78.9296 MiB/s on the medium-track condition at observability level 3 (n = 150, CV 15.3%); the paper makes no superiority claim.
Ciphertext expansion on fixture tracks was an exact, zero-variance 1.7113.
Length is not hidden exactly: non-sealed levels disclose byte_length in the manifest, and sealed export still reveals the PADMÉ bucket.
Concludes that a flat ZIP container can carry typed multimodal tracks, authenticated encryption, graded observability and proof export without becoming a repository or hosted service.
